results.fact: Best/safest month on the Mary Green Glacier (bergschrund/crevasse timing)
results.correct_value: Early to mid July is the best window; from late July the glacier breaks up and the moat/bergschrund gets harder, with August-September still possible (more so in low-snow years).
results.evidence: A July 13-14, 2024 ascent report states early to mid-July is the best time to keep the bergschrund crossing simple while the upper scramble is snow-free. The route's main description says it is best climbed mid-summer before the glacier gets so broken up that the glacier-to-rock transition becomes an issue, and that most climbers find good conditions in July. A late-July 2003 report adds that later in the season the moat crossing is harder with steeper ice. seasonal_guidance (August optimal) and crowds.peakTraffic (August as when the bergschrund is easiest) were the outliers against season, best_season, climate, watch_out, crevasses and itinerary.cal.

results.correct_value: Holden Village / Railroad Creek approach in the North Cascades (Glacier Peak Wilderness); Bonanza is Washington's highest non-volcanic peak and the Chelan County highpoint.
results.evidence: Bonanza Peak is in the North Cascades in the Glacier Peak Wilderness, the highest non-volcanic peak in Washington and Chelan County's highpoint (encyclopedia entry; county-highpoint and peak-listing pages agree). Documented ascents approach from Holden Village via the Railroad Creek and Holden Lake trails to Holden Lake/Holden Pass and the Mary Green Glacier (2003 and 2024 reports). Nothing places it in the Wenatchee Mountains or near the Middle Fork Snoqualmie.

patches.fact: Which trailhead/range this route describes
patches.expect: Bonanza Peak is the highest point in the Wenatchee Mountains, a popular mountaineering objective. The North Ridge is the most direct approach to the summit, a straightforward Class 2 scramble over talus and low-angle rock with good routefinding.
patches.value: Bonanza Peak is the highest non-volcanic summit in Washington and the Chelan County highpoint, deep in the Glacier Peak Wilderness above Holden Village. This line is the peak's standard east-side route: roped travel up the Mary Green Glacier, then loose Class 3-4 scrambling through a gully/rib system to a notch on the upper northeast ridge and a short, exposed crest to the summit.

patches.fact: Which trailhead/range this route describes
patches.expect: From the Middle Fork Snoqualmie trailhead, approach via the alpine meadows to the north ridge base. Follow the ridge crest, staying on solid rock and stable talus. Most routefinding is straightforward and well-marked by cairns. Descend the same route.
patches.value: From Holden Village, hike the Railroad Creek and Holden Lake trails to camp at Holden Lake or Holden Pass. Cross the Mary Green Glacier to the rock, weave between the two gully/rib lines to the notch on the upper ridge, and follow the crest to the summit. Descend the same route.

results.fact: Total elevation gain/loss for the route
results.correct_value: ~6,300 ft car to car (about 3,000 ft Holden Village to camp + about 3,300 ft camp to summit). gain_ft/loss_ft 6300 are right; itinerary day-1 4,000 ft and the '~7,500'' claim are the errors.
results.evidence: Holden Village sits near 3,300 ft, Holden Pass near 6,360 ft and the summit at 9,511 ft (2003 report), about 3,060 ft to camp and 3,150 ft to the summit. A 2021 report gives 3,000 ft Holden to camp and 3,100 ft camp to summit, and a GPS-tracked 2018 trip logged 6,750 ft total; none supports 7,300-7,500 ft. The NE Buttress leaves the same camp for the same summit with no intervening descent, and the row's own waypoints (3,262 -> 6,400 -> 8,350 -> 9,516, monotonic) give ~6,250 ft net. The reader's internal resolution was reversed: day-1 gainFt 4,000 (and the matching day-3 lossFt) and the approach prose's '~7,500'' are the outliers.

results.fact: Best window for the glacier approach (July vs August)
results.correct_value: Early to mid July for the easiest Mary Green Glacier margin and bergschrund; the buttress rock tolerates a later start into August as the glacier breaks up.
results.evidence: best_season and approach_variants[0].season say late June to mid-July is easiest for the glacier with August tolerable for the rock, but itinerary.cal says best mid-to-late July and seasonal_guidance calls August optimal because the glacier's crevasses and snow bridges are 'most stable' then. This route crosses the same Mary Green Glacier as the standard line: a 2024 report puts the best bergschrund timing in early to mid-July, and the route's main description says it is best before the glacier gets broken up mid-summer, with a late-July 2003 report noting the moat gets harder later. So August is not the most stable glacier month.

results.fact: CAMPING & BIVY options listed for this route
results.evidence: The bivy array is the identical nine-camp zone list stored on every route in this zone (the Bonanza North Ridge row carries the same nine entries in the same order), and no entry claims Buckskin is reached from Holden; each describes its own camp accurately, and the Ice Lakes entry covers the Entiat corridor. The Entiat approach itself is confirmed (2018 and 2020 reports use the Entiat River Trail and camp in upper Entiat Meadows). Trimming the list for one route is a data-model decision (zone list vs per-route list), not a factual correction; the real gap is that the Entiat Meadows camp is missing from it.

results.correct_value: No avalanche concern in the Jul-Sep window, but May-June ascents meet steep icy snow and cornices on the south-face avalanche path, with wet-slide potential.
results.evidence: A May 16, 2020 ascent found icy snow needing crampons above about 4,300 ft, front-pointing on the upper ridge and large cornices on the east ridge. A June 21-23, 2020 party needed crampons on icy snow to reach the east ridge at 7,200 ft, while a late-July 2018 party found the same south-side rib snow-free and describes the face as a big open avalanche slope. This agrees with the row's obj_haz, climate.spring and May-June crampons; the avalanche zone text's blanket N/A was the outlier. byMonth (Jul-Sep N/A) is left as is.
